newsitem.title: USA: Education Alternatives sees final Hartford pact.
newsitem.headline: Education Alternatives sees final Hartford pact.

text.p: Education Alternatives Inc said on Friday it expects to finalize its agreement with Hartford, Conn., officials in the near future.
As previously reported, Education Alternatives and Hartford officials reached a preliminary agreement related to the cancellation of the company's school management contract.
The company said it has accepted an additional $3,250,000 to be paid by Hartford in equal annual installments over the next five years, which will bring the total Hartford settlement to $6.3 million.

On Thursday, Education Alternatives reported a loss for its first quarter ended September 30 of $0.02 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.34. Revenue for the quarter was $747,000, compared with $30,532,000 last year.

The company said revenue for this year consists primarily of tuition from its two private schools. Prior year results included revenues and expenses from Baltimore, Md., and Hartford school management and consulting contracts.

Results for the first quarter included settlement proceeds of $625,000 received from its investment management firm, which has agreed to pay the company $1,250,000 to resolve all remaining issues related to management of the investment portfolio.
The remaining settlment proceeds of $625,000 will be recorded in income during fiscal 1997 when they are received.

"As we move forward, our efforts will be focused on those private and public school opportunities where we can control our own performance, both educationally and financially," John Golle, chairman, said in a statement. "We have shown that we can provide, in different environments, a quality educational experience in a cost-effective manner."
